requirements.syllabus_text: discuss the aims of government policy and why they should be achieved - full employment - prevention of inflation - economic growth - redistribution of income - balance of payments stability

requirements.gap: No card on confidentiality of status, no compulsory testing, counselling/information; Namibian law basis (Labour Act 2007 s5) not stated
requirements.why: V basic cards plus J confidentiality evaluation (moved to extended).

requirements.demand: Define; calculate index from basket; interpret changes; weights
requirements.adequate_response: Index = current basket cost/base cost x100; points vs percent; weights in basket

topic_summaries.strengths_V: Clear 2-mark definitions for all aims, policies and taxes; real Namibian tax examples (income tax, company tax, VAT, excise); V-P03 fiscal/monetary business case; V-P04 9-mark evaluate matching exam pattern.
topic_summaries.strengths_J: Numeric tax-rate templates (5%/10%, 10%/2%, 3.33%); transfer cases (net employment, tax-cut leakage, disinflation, import leakage); cleaner misconception wording; short-answer bundle J-P01 with consistent marking.
topic_summaries.defects_V: Marking for definition cards offers two marks where answer holds one idea; V-018 (fixed-rate loans) off-target; 'relevant' wording overused; many near-duplicates (V-007/008/009/032, V-010, V-033, V-031); V-P01 and V-P02 weak.
topic_summaries.defects_J: Peg and teacher meta-language injected into cards 017, 018, 032, 033; three 7-mark EVAL cards on flashcards; J-037 off-topic; duplicates of V definitions; 14-mark assessments off-pattern; J-P02 over-engineered.

topic_summaries.coherence: Order: policy, aims, fiscal/monetary, taxes, budget, interest rate. Terminology consistent within bank. Peg remarks only in J and not in syllabus; inconsistent depth of Namibian content.
topic_summaries.notes_vs_cards: V notes (6.2) say Bank follows SARB because of peg and give example tax rates as non-Namibian; cards consistent. J notes require analysis to respect the peg; J cards add that rider mechanically, which the notes do not require on every card.
nonverified_claims: NAD pegged 1:1 to rand; BoN policy framed around protecting the peg: verified by web search 2026-11-08, latest decision found Dec 2025 (6.5% repo); no 2026 decision found
Namibia not matching SARB's 2022 hikes (IMF coverage, one source)
Tax types in Namibia (personal income tax, company tax, VAT, excise): standard, not checked against current tax law; V cards avoid rates
Namibia old-age pension and grants as redistribution (from 2023 P2 extract only)

topic_summaries.strengths_V: Three correct, image-checked supply/demand diagrams (max price, min price, min wage) matching the best-evidenced exam topic (2020 P2 Q1); minimum-wage misconception card; HIV non-discrimination cards; V-P03 integrated case; V notes rich in Namibian institutions.
topic_summaries.strengths_J: Externality and information-asymmetry reasons for intervention; enforcement-gap card; HIV confidentiality evaluation.
topic_summaries.defects_V: Cards are generic and name no Namibian law/institution though notes do; template residue ('household/workers'); 'Draw' on a flashcard; V-009 unverifiable; V-P01, V-P02 weak.
topic_summaries.defects_J: Only 10 items, three of them 7-mark EVAL flashcards with thin answers; no diagrams, no minimum wage or price control content; Namibia-specific content absent from cards.

topic_summaries.notes_vs_cards: V notes name Labour Act (HIV status prohibited ground), NaCC, NSI, NAMFISA, CRAN and cover monopoly and subsidies; V cards omit them, so cards under-test the notes. J notes shorter, cards consistent.
